text:
maya: heads up, trying to onboard a HF checkpoint (repo uses custom_arch + trust_remote_code). auto_map is silently returning base classes and tokenizer seems to lose special tokens after conversion.

maya: steps i ran: `transformers==4.32`, `safetensors` load, `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True, device_map='auto')` then our hf->redwood converter.

maya: after conversion, generation looks fine for short prompts but fails for continuation: weird tokenization on leading spaces and [CLS] like tokens appearing. example: `model.generate(tokenizer.encode(" hello"))` produces garbled past-kv and misaligned logits.

tj: @maya can you paste the tokenizer config.json? suspicious that special_tokens_map or added_tokens not preserved.

maya: sure, here's the tokenizer.json chunk we get post-conversion:
```json
"special_tokens_map": {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "unk_token": "<unk>"},
"added_tokens": [{"id": 50277, "content": "<special_tok>"}]
```

maya: but the HF original had bos as null and forced `pad_token` set to `<pad>` in a separate config class that only appears when trust_remote_code instantiates custom tokenizer. converter seems to drop that.

jorge: did you hit auto_map warnings in logs? when transformers sees an unknown module it prints a `trust_remote_code` warning and auto_map fallback messages. our converter expects the config class name to match one of the builtin map keys.

maya: yep, logs show: `UserWarning: Falling back to AutoConfig for class CustomConfig because it's not in auto_map` then `converter: no custom handler, using GenericConfig`.

sophia: for quant experiments this is ugly — if pad/bos change, kv cache indexing goes out and quantized kernels amplify errors. which quant backend did you test? int8 on triton?

maya: tested int8 on our custom triton path and q4_k_m on CPU. int8 shows immediate hallucinations after 30 tokens; full fp16 mostly okay.

tj: quick suggestions: 1) dump the HF model's `config.json` and the custom class source (from remote repo) so we can mirror fields, 2) run `tokenizer.save_pretrained(tmp)` and compare `vocab`, `added_tokens.json` and `special_tokens_map.json`, 3) try forcing `pad_token` to `<pad>` before conversion and run unit test.

maya: did that. forcing pad token pre-conversion keeps generation stable for a bit but then oddities reappear when we enable continuous batching — suspect mismatch in `is_split_into_words` or `do_normalize` flags from custom tokenizer.

jorge: continuous batching interacts with prefix KV caching. If the tokenizer changes leading-space handling, cache keys differ and we attach wrong pasts. can you reproduce with a minimal script that toggles `use_cache`?

maya: reproducer attached inline:
```py
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
 tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('repo/custom', trust_remote_code=True)
 model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('repo/custom', trust_remote_code=True)
 tok.pad_token = '<pad>'
 inputs = tok(["hello"," hello"], return_tensors='pt', padding=True)
 out = model.generate(**inputs, do_sample=False, use_cache=True, max_new_tokens=40)
```

maya: output divergence between the two inputs is huge even though they differ only by leading space.

tj: thanks. next steps: (a) @infra-bot can you pin a test job to run this on a dedicated GPU so we can see triton kernels + nvprof traces? (b) @jorge can you inspect our hf->redwood converter for logic that drops `pad_token` when using GenericConfig? (c) @sophia please run quantized kernels with forced tokenizer flags and report regression metrics.

infra-bot: job queued: hg-onboard-1769801234 (gpu-dedicated), link: https://ci.redwood/jobs/1769801234

jorge: I'll add a small patch to preserve `special_tokens_map` and `added_tokens` by copying any fields present in `tokenizer.json` even when class unknown. will open PR and include unit test.

sophia: running quant buckets now, will post recall/rep rate after 10k prompts. initial quickcheck shows int8 false positive rate jumps ~12% on leading-space prompt set.

maya: thanks all. plan: keep trust_remote_code for this model until we implement a custom converter handler. if we can't reproduce without remote code we'll block onboard and mark as non-compatible for auto-quant. 

tj: agree. add an entry to the model registry: flag `requires_trust_remote_code: true` and `autoconvert: manual_review`. that will prevent accidental auto-deploy. :white_check_mark:
